initial_doctor_view.public_context: I am a 69-year-old male farmer with poorly controlled type 2 diabetes mellitus and irritable bowel syndrome. I come for a routine check-up.
initial_doctor_view.request_rule: Examinations in unavailable_exams cannot be requested again in this encounter; their findings stay unknown, not normal or negative. Rephrasing a blocked request does not make it available. An identical question is not answered twice. Once the patient says there is nothing more to add, further history questions return nothing. A blocked attempt still spends one action. For a compound request, omit its blocked part and request the rest separately.
initial_doctor_view.task: Determine the most likely diagnosis of the scalp lesion at the follow-up visit.

facts.text: I was instructed to monitor my blood glucose. Three months later, I returned because a wound on my scalp had not healed.

exams.text:
Initial examination reveals a scalp lesion (Figure A).
The current scalp examination reveals the finding shown in Figure B.
Unlabeled image from the case file. The source does not state its modality or body site.

events.query: Examine the scalp lesion for appearance, size, drainage, and signs of infection.

trace.reasoning:
The patient is a 69-year-old male farmer with a history of a non-healing scalp wound. Image A displays a rough, erythematous plaque with significant hyperkeratosis and a collarette of scale, which is the classic presentation of actinic keratosis. Image B shows a crusted, ulcerated lesion, representing the progression of the lesion to squamous cell carcinoma. While the patient's diabetes (Option B) causes poor healing, the specific morphology of the lesion in Image A is pathognomonic for actinic keratosis, and the evolution to the ulcerated state in Image B confirms the diagnosis of squamous cell carcinoma. Basal cell carcinoma (Option C) typically presents with pearly borders, and melanoma (Option D) with pigmentary changes, neither of which are the primary features here. Therefore, the lesion represents a squamous cell carcinoma arising from an actinic keratosis.

Squamous cell carcinoma

final_choices.B: Poor wound healing secondary to diabetes
